evidence.note: availableInMs repeats consume's cost validation and refill-then-shortfall arithmetic, returning 0 when the balance covers the cost and a ceil-rounded delay otherwise; formula matches consume's retryAfterMs.
peek delegates to refill and returns its token count, so it reports without spending and the JSDoc contract at lines 83-88 holds.
refill caps the balance at capacity on the elapsed-time branch and leaves the new-bucket path at capacity; consume, sweep and availableInMs all depend on this being bounded.
consume validates cost the same way availableInMs does and already clamps deltas; the two computation paths agree for affordable and unaffordable costs.

New tests cover the zero-delay affordable case, the rounded-up delay for a depleted bucket, regained tokens, and repeated calls not spending when affordable, with peek(10) asserting the balance is intact.
Covers the unaffordable non-spend path via peek(3) and the three rejection cases (0, -1, cost above capacity), matching consume's validation contract.
Existing peek-at-capacity, refill-over-time and never-past-capacity assertions still exercise the repaired peek and refill paths and would fail if either regression returned.
